problem_statement: Problem 2.3 (Expanders). Prove that all vertex-transitive expanders exhibit cutoff. Random walks on groups. One place where vertex-transitive graphs arise naturally is group theory: let X be a finite group and let S ⊆X be a set of elements that generates the group. By definition, the Cayley graph G = Cay(X, S) is the graph with vertex set VG = X and edge set EG = {(x, sx): x ∈X, s ∈S}. This graph is vertex-transitive, since for any (x, y) ∈X2 the map σxy : z 7→zx−1y is an edge-preserving bijection that sends x to y.

Conjecture 8.1 (Bubble hypothesis) (a) Almost surely, there does not exist an infinite sequence of points (z_k)_{k>=0} in S* union M*, all different from each other, such that phi(z_{k-1}) = z_k for all k >= 1. (b) Almost surely, there does not exist an infinite sequence of points (z_k) in S* union M*, all different, such that phi(z_k) = z_{k-1} for all k >= 1.

problem_statement: '(6) The Brownian web has been shown by Ellis and Feldheim to be a two-dimensional black noise, equipped with a family of sub-sigma-fields indexed by finite unions of open rectangles in R^2. Is there a maximal extension of the family of sub-sigma-fields, indexed by a Boolean algebra of domains in R^2 that include the rectangles, such that the Brownian web remains a noise? A similar question is also open for the scaling limit of critical planar percolation. Recently Tsirelson showed by general arguments that there exists some continuous path f starting at time -infinity, such that F_{f-} and F_{f+}, the sigma-fields generated by Brownian web paths restricted respectively to the left or the right of the graph of f, do not jointly generate the full sigma-field F. Can we characterize the set of f for which the factorization property F = F_{f-} v F_{f+} holds? (The case f = 0 has been treated by Ellis-Feldheim.)'
title: Maximal noise structure of the Brownian web and the factorisation set

problem_statement: '(8) The Brownian web appears in the scaling limit of super-critical oriented percolation, as discussed in Section 7.2.6, and the Brownian net is expected to arise if the percolation parameter p is allowed to vary in a small interval. However, the most interesting question is: What is the scaling limit of critical (and near-critical) oriented percolation (OP) on Z^{1+1}? The Brownian net with killing provides a simpler model to study the OP universality class. We expect that in the near-critical scaling limit, one would obtain a family of models which interpolates between the Brownian net and the scaling limit of critical oriented percolation. However, such a goal appears far out of reach at the moment, because there are no conjectures at all on what the critical scaling limit might be, and neither have critical exponents been shown to exist.'
title: Scaling limit of critical and near-critical oriented percolation in 1+1 dimensions

problem_statement: Conjecture 9 (Benjamini, Kalai, and Schramm (1999)). (i) Let f be a Boolean function described by a monotone threshold circuit of size M and depth D. problem_statement: [Verbatim from the source, Section 3.3.4.] Consider n steps simple random walk (SRW) X_n on a Cayley graph of a finitely generated infinite group Gamma. Refresh independently each step with probability epsilon, to get Y_n from X_n. Are there groups for which the positions at time n, X_n and Y_n are asymptotically independent? That is, the l_1 (total variation) distance between the chain (X_n, Y_n) and two independent copies (X'_n, X''_n) is going to 0, with n. Note that on the line Z, they are uniformally correlated, and therefore also on any group with a non trivial homomorphism to R, or any group that has a finite index subgroup with a non trivial homomorphism to R. On the free group and for any non-Liouville group, X_n and Y_n are correlated as well, but for a different reason: Both X_n and Y_n have nontrivial correlation with X_1. Itai Benjamini and Jeremie Brieussel conjecture that these are the only ways not to be noise sensitive. That is, if a Cayley graph is Liouville and the group does not have a finite index subgroup with a homomorphism to the reals, then the Cayley graph is noise sensitive for the simple random walk. In particular, the Grigorchuk group is noise sensitive for the simple random walk!
title: Noise sensitivity of simple random walk on Liouville Cayley graphs

problem_statement: [Verbatim from the source, Section 3.3.3.] Consider an infinite planar grid where every edge is assigned a length: 1 with probability 1/2 and 2 with probability 1/2 (independently). This model of a random metric on the planar grid is called first-passage percolation. An old question is to understand what is the variance V(n) of the distance D from (0,0) to (n,0)? Now, let M be the median value of D and consider the Boolean function f describing the event 'D >= M'. Is f noise sensitive? Benjamini, Kalai and Schramm (2003) showed, more or less, that f is sensitive to logarithmic level of noise, and concluded that V(n) = O(n/log n). (The argument uses hypercontractivity and is similar to the argument for critical planar percolation.) To show that f is sensitive to noise level of n^delta for delta > 0 would imply that V(n) = O(n^{1-c}). A very interesting question is whether methods used for critical planar percolation for obtaining stronger noise sensitivity results can also be applied here.
title: Noise sensitivity of the event that the first-passage distance exceeds its median

problem_statement: Consider the group G = {-1, 1}^N, and denote by lambda its Haar measure. Denote by mu a 'biased coin' measure on G. This is a product measure with identical factors that gives different weights to 1 and -1, or, equivalently, this is the law of an infinite sequence of trials obtained by flipping a biased coin. Problem. Prove that there is function phi : R_+ -> R_+ such that lim_{t -> infinity} t phi(t) = 0 and, for all f on G with f >= 0 and integral f dlambda = 1, and all t >= 0, lambda({f * mu >= t}) <= phi(t). Of course, f is assumed to be measurable. The meaning of this statement is that convolution by a biased coin smooths a function, in the sense that the convolution never looks like a 'peak function' (1/lambda(A)) 1_A for lambda(A) small. Of course the function phi will depend on mu. [Source: 'A conjecture on convolution operators, and operators from L^1 to a Banach lattice', Israel J. Math. 68 (1989); the constant N is arbitrary and phi must not depend on N.]
title: Talagrand's convolution conjecture on the discrete cube

problem_statement: Question 6.2. In Z^2, is the limiting shape of S_{n,H} as n -> infinity a regular (4H+12)-gon? [Same page: 'Simulations indicate that for general H >= -2, the limiting shape of S_{n,H} in Z^2 may be a polygon with 4H + 12 sides.' 'Simulations indicate a regular (4H + 12)-gon with some rounding at the corners; it remains unclear if the rounded portions of the boundary become negligible in the limit. Even if the limiting shape is not a polygon, it would still be very interesting to establish the weaker statement that it has the dihedral symmetry D_{4H+12}.' Figure 11: square, octagon and dodecagon for H = -2, -1, 0.] [Setting, Section 6, PDF p. 29: 'Fey-den Boer and Redig [FR07] consider aggregation in the sandpile model on Z^d. In their setup, the underlying graph for the chip-firing game is the infinite undirected d-dimensional cubic lattice Z^d. Start with each site containing h <= 2d - 2 chips. Here h may be even be taken negative, corresponding to starting with a hole of depth H = -h at each lattice site; that is, each site absorbs the first H chips it receives, and thereafter fires every time it receives an additional four chips. Now add n chips to the origin and stabilize. Denote by S_{n,H} the set of sites in Z^d which fired in the process of stabilization.' Theorem 6.1 ([FR07]): S_{n,2-2d} is a cube C(r_n) for every n; in Z^2, S_{n,-2} is a square. PDF p. 30: 'even the existence of a limiting shape for S_{n,H} has not been proved in the case H > -2', and as H -> infinity the limiting shape is a ball (Fey-Redig; Theorem 6.3 of Levine-Peres).]
title: Is the sandpile aggregate on a background of holes a regular (4H+12)-gon?

problem_statement: Conjecture 7.1: For any tau such that chi(tau) > -infinity, chi(tau) = chi*(tau). [Same page: 'The conjecture (named unification problem by D. Voiculescu [129])'.] [Setting, Chapter 7, PDF pp. 80-81: tau in M(m) is a tracial law of m non-commutative self-adjoint variables; chi(tau) is Voiculescu's microstates free entropy (defined through the volume of sets of m-tuples of N x N Hermitian matrices whose empirical distribution approximates tau); Phi*(tau) = sum_i ||D*_{X_i} 1||^2_{L^2(tau)} is the free Fisher information and chi*(tau) = -(1/2) int_0^1 Phi*(tau_t^b) dt (with tau_t^b the law of (t X_i + sqrt(t(1-t)) S_i), S_i free semicirculars free from X) is the non-microstates free entropy, up to the source's normalisation; Theorem 7.3 ([18], Biane-Capitaine-Guionnet): chi(tau) <= chi*(tau) for every tau. Remark 7.2: 'If the conjecture would hold for any tau in M(m) and not only for tau with finite microstates entropy, it would provide an affirmative answer to Connes question since it is known that if tau is the law of X_1, ..., X_m and S_1, ..., S_m free semicircular variables, free with X_1, ..., X_m then, for any epsilon > 0 the distribution tau_epsilon of (X_1 + epsilon S_1, ..., X_m + epsilon S_m) satisfies chi*(tau_epsilon) > -infinity, and hence the above equality would imply chi(tau_epsilon) > -infinity so that one could find matrices whose empirical distribution approximates tau_epsilon and thus tau since epsilon can be chosen arbitrarily small.']

problem_statement: Bernoulli bond percolation with parameter p on a finite graph G = (V,E), o in V, B a subset of V. An event A is increasing with respect to the percolation configuration if omega -> P[A | pi = omega] is increasing on {0,1}^E (pi the configuration; the event may depend on extra randomness). Conjecture 2.2. There exists a universal function phi : (0, +infinity) -> R, independent of G, o, B and p, such that phi(eps) -> 1 as eps -> 0, and such that the following statement always holds. Let eps > 0. Let (E_b)_{b in B} be a family of events which are increasing with respect to the percolation configuration. Assume that P[E_b] >= 1 - eps for every b in B. Then P[ union_{b in B} ({o <-> b} cap E_b) ] >= phi(eps) P[o <-> B]. [Theorem 2.4 of the source: the conjecture implies theta(p_c) = 0 for every d >= 2, via Kozma and Nitzan's Theorem 6.]
